attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The draft drops 'LLM' before profits. As written, 'profits outside Nvidia are scarce' is much broader than 'LLM profits outside of Nvidia are hard to find'. The contract restores the LLM scope. The commodity and OpenAI-loss parts are faithful.

contract.note: An informed reader takes 'losing billions every month' as an ongoing monthly run rate. Requiring verified losses for each separate month, and refusing the quarterly average, stretches the words against the speaker. Requiring a stated accounting basis the speaker never gave also cuts against him. The commodity and profit parts are read fairly.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure of the after-tax hit from its OpenAI stake for Jul–Sep 2025. This is Microsoft's figure, not OpenAI's net loss.
A press reconstruction implying about $4.2B a month on average. It rests on an assumed proportional allocation and is an estimate, not reported monthly figures.
An April 2025 OpenRouter study finding model differentiation. It predates the target period and does not settle whether LLMs were commoditised later.

reviews.rationale: This is a three-part claim. The press estimate suggests OpenAI's losses averaged several billion dollars a month, which fits a fair run-rate reading, but it is a reconstruction, not a reported figure. The packet has no adequate evidence on whether LLMs were commoditised or whether LLM profits outside Nvidia were scarce. So the evidence does not settle the claim as a whole.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: Nearly verbatim, keeping the subjective qualifier. 'Too much' and 'too little' are judgments; the testable core is causal: uncritical hype drove up valuations.

contract.note: Requiring causal evidence that separates hype amplification from fundamentals is a fair test of the causal core. The period inferred from his examples is reasonable.

evidence.note: The Bank of England notes stretched AI valuations and points to earnings as one driver. It does not identify media hype as a cause.
A 2005–2018 study of corporate filings, not media coverage. Different period and mechanism, so it neither supports nor contradicts the claim.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet identifies a causal effect of uncritical hype amplification on valuations in 2023–2025. Elevated valuations alone do not establish the mechanism, and the filings study covers a different period and channel. The evidence does not settle it either way.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Faithful to both clauses, including 'the full solution people imagine'. The second clause is partly evaluative.

contract.note: Reading 'partial solution' as an architectural point — the model is one component in a system with external tools — follows Marcus's own argument, which links the two clauses. That reading decides the result. It does not test any claim about AGI sufficiency, and 'resorted' (implying necessity) cannot be verified.

evidence.note: OpenAI, March 2023: ChatGPT models were given a real Python interpreter in a sandbox, with math listed as a use case. Executing code, not just writing it.
Anthropic, May 2025: code execution, MCP connectors, file storage and web search offered around Claude. Shows multiple external tools at a second provider.

reviews.rationale: Dated provider documentation shows LLM systems integrated external code execution and other tools within 2022–2025, with the model as one part of a larger system. Under the contract's architectural reading, both clauses hold. The evidence does not show tools were strictly necessary.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'almost all' and the universal 'every single model since'. Naming the earlier predictions about GPT-4 matches the surrounding text.

contract.note: The contract keeps his universal scope and correctly excludes the future-AGI-architecture prediction from being confirmed by current limits. How the predictions are counted is not specified, which shapes any verdict.

evidence.note: Anthropic's June 2025 stress tests found misaligned behaviour in models from six families. This partly supports the alignment prediction only, in artificial scenarios, and predates GPT-5.
OpenAI's 2024 schema-compliance guarantee shows narrow progress on output format. It does not settle broader reliability.

reviews.rationale: The packet supports persistent alignment failures across several model families, but nothing covers most prediction categories or every model since GPT-4. The structured-outputs evidence is narrow progress, not a refutation. Coverage is too thin to settle 'almost all' across 'every single model'.
